name: Pam Tillis
notes: The wry, jazz-touched pole of 90s female country — "a flexible mezzo over a band that swings more than it drives". She is claimed by this section rather than by `country-train` for a documented reason: nineteen reachable readings (the most complete tempo distribution in either archetype section) put her identity in the 106–128 mid-shuffle band, and the research flags "the 123-BPM triple point (three separate singles), which is the strongest single anchor for the mid honky-tonk shuffle in the batch" — so bpm.mode is 123, taken straight from that anchor rather than from a centre calculation. Drums are the entry's: "the 106–128 band runs a shuffled two-beat with the lope on a closed hat, dry snare, kick on 1 and 3; the torch material uses brushes or cross-stick in a slow swung feel", and "'Mi Vida Loca' swaps the shuffle for a Latin percussion pattern (congas and a clave-referenced kick) which the engine should treat as an alternate preset rather than a variation" — so this kit is the shuffle only. Its kick restates country-shuffle's own values unchanged (densityPerBar 2–3, anchors 1 and 3, syncopation 0.14); the single departure from the parent is offbeat8thShare 0.08 → 0.10 for the shuffled two-beat, and the percs are the rim (cross-stick) and ride lanes with no conga in them. The alternate preset is recorded rather than encoded, and deliberately not authored as a `modes` entry: her entry documents it as percussion and tempo only ("one Latin-flavoured outlier at 180", "accordion and mariachi-adjacent colours on the Latin cut"), so a mode built from what is actually written would change no pitch, and `engine/tests/modes.rs::two_moods_of_one_artist_do_not_generate_the_same_thing` requires two moods to generate different melodies — passing it would mean inventing a harmonic difference the entry never states. Authoring modes would also replace the three moods this model inherits from country-shuffle, one of which (cross-stick verse) is the torch treatment her own entry documents. Harmony is the entry's own and is deeper than the radio norm: ii–V–I cycles, secondary dominants (the VI–ii–V turnaround), 6th and 9th voicings on the swing-leaning cuts, I–IV–V with V7 on the honky-tonk cuts, and a torch **iv borrow** — which is authored as `borrowed.iv` at 0.25 rather than as a family, because a borrowed chord is a quality swap on a degree the family already has. The vocal is the documented "agile mezzo with jazz-inflected phrasing — back-phrased entries, notes held across chord changes, conversational verses opening to a wide sustained chorus", so the melody is legato with a low chord-tone bias (0.68) and long 4–8-bar phrases. The entry also notes that "several cuts use a genuine bridge rather than letting the solo do that job, which distinguishes her from the honky-tonk names here", which is why both structures carry a bridge. ⚠ INFERRED: swing.amount 0.66, all velocity tiers, ghost probability and vel, hat and percs densities, and the 0.25 borrow probability. The BPM readings are bpmdatabase values, [LOW-CONF] as a class, and the research marks the harmonic sophistication as inferred from the swing/torch repertoire [LOW-CONF].
